_comment: PROVIDER PLUG-IN for the `real-data-controls` role — the KEEP-IT-OUT shape: the real value never enters the application store at all. A token vault holds it, the workload handles a surrogate, and getting the real value back is a separate, individually authorised, individually logged detokenisation call. It closes the same hole as the encrypt-in-place shape from the other end — instead of protecting the data where the agents and engineers already are, it removes the data from where they are. It PROTECTS nothing by itself and verifies no read: the harness reads JSON records and never watches production. To adopt: record the choice in docs/governance/provider-selection.json, copy this file to docs/governance/adapters/, point it at your vault and its audit log, and wire the fetch that fills activation_evidence.
capability: Substitution of customer-identifying values with non-reversible surrogates held by a token vault, so application stores, fixtures, logs and agent context carry tokens only, with every detokenisation authorised and recorded by the vault

role_fit._comment: Stated plainly so the choice is made with open eyes. Neither line argues for or against — they are the trade being accepted.
role_fit.strength: The blast radius collapses to one system. A dump of an application database, a debug log, a fixture accidentally committed, or a prompt carrying a customer record contains surrogates and nothing else — which is the failure mode this bundle spends the most effort on elsewhere, here removed rather than guarded. It also keeps the synthetic-only posture true for most of the estate, so pii-guard.sh and the fixture conventions stay meaningful after the move to real data
role_fit.limitation: IT MOVES THE SURFACE, IT DOES NOT REMOVE IT. The detokenisation endpoint is now the whole control, and it is a single high-value target that must authorise per call rather than per session — a broad grant there recreates the plaintext estate in one hop. It also breaks what the other shape preserves: joins, uniqueness assumptions, format-dependent validation and analytics all have to be reworked against surrogates, which is where projects quietly widen the grant to make a report run

reconciliation._comment: NO SHIPPED GATE READS THIS ARTIFACT, and `gate_mechanism` is null rather than naming one. REAL-PII-SURFACE is catalogued `absent`: the harness ships nothing for the real-data case, which is the whole reason this role exists. scripts/adapter-evidence-check.mjs is the nearest thing and it is NOT it — it reads signed observations under docs/governance/adapter-evidence/, not this path, and it makes no claim at all about an adapter outside the stream contract (core/floor-adapters.mjs `isStreamAdapter`), which this one is. What the harness DOES see is that a provider was selected (PS-R06) and whether activation_evidence is still placeholders (adapter-check.mjs). So the reconciliation below is the ADOPTER'S, performed by the fetch that fills activation_evidence. `residual_plaintext_stores` is the field that earns this adapter its keep: tokenisation projects are judged on what was tokenised; what decides the exposure is what was NOT, and that list is the one nobody publishes. Reconcile on it and a store left holding plaintext is a finding rather than an omission — but note WHOSE finding, because nothing in CI will raise it for you. WHAT A GATE WOULD TAKE: this envelope committed as a signed observation under docs/governance/adapter-evidence/ naming REAL-PII-SURFACE, asserted by an issuer outside the coding agent's write scope, with the denial as a required negative — plus a data-custody mechanism in SEAM_MECHANISMS, which carries none today, and a gate that reads it.
reconciliation.reconciled_by: the adopter's fetch and negative probe — no gate in this harness

activation_evidence._comment: ADOPT: fill from a real vault read + the negative probe. detokenisations_authorised proves the vault is in the path, never that it refuses anyone. Only a denial you provoked and then found in the VAULT's own log shows the control bit.
activation_evidence.fetched_at: ADOPT: timestamp of your vault and audit-log read
activation_evidence.asserted_by: ADOPT: the vault / audit-log service identity that emits these records — must NOT be the application or agent that detokenises through them
activation_evidence.negative_probe: ADOPT: 'denied-and-logged' once an identity WITHOUT detokenisation rights has attempted a call, been refused, and that refusal has been found in the vault's audit log
activation_evidence.residual_probe: ADOPT: 'enumerated' once the stores still holding plaintext have been listed and each one has an owner and a dated plan — an empty list asserted without a survey is the claim this field exists to prevent
